Hi Amelia — thanks again for your time today. Great to meet the CardioSys team and walk through the demo focused on low-latency inference for clinical triage. Per our discussion, you flagged two primary constraints from Legal & Security: (1) minimum PII retention window of 0–6 hours for PHI sessions, and (2) strict residency requirement that logs remain in a US-only region.

Recap of actionable items we committed to: 
- Triage: provide a short one-page summary of Redwood retention/config options for ephemeral sessions (attached).
- Security ask: confirm technical feasibility of a 2-hour KV/log TTL and describe audit-evidence we can provide (SOC2 excerpts, access logs).
- Contract: sketch an initial Minimal Operational Plan (MOP) that includes a short-retain carveout and fallback policy.

I attached a quick retention-options summary and a blank MOP draft to speed review. Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll follow up with a feasibility note from Karthik on TTL enforcement and audit evidence by EOD tomorrow (4/6).
2) If that looks good, we can prepare a concise contract addendum that captures the carveout and acceptance criteria.
3) Schedule a short call with your security reviewer to walk the evidence.

Would Friday 4/9 10:00am PT work for a 30-minute security sync? If not, please suggest two windows.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap and for the docs. Quick clarifications from Security & Legal (copied):

- The 0–6 hour window is a target; Legal is most comfortable with "no persistent storage beyond immediate processing" for PHI unless we have a strong audit trail showing access controls + retention enforcement.
- For residency: CardioSys requires data-at-rest for any logs to remain solely in our US tenant (us-west region). That includes any KV cache snapshots we might need for warm starts.
- Audit evidence: we need to see (a) example log lines (redacted) showing retention truncation, (b) SOC2 excerpt demonstrating log retention policy, and (c) a sample access log export for a 24h window.

Also, procurement has asked whether a short-term trial with strict logging (2h TTL) is possible before committing to a reserved plan. That would be a strong path for us.

Can you confirm these three items are on your side and share the requested artifacts? If feasible, we’re happy to do the security sync Friday 4/9 10am PT.

Best — Amelia

Tessa / Ben — quick technical readout for Amelia and Security:

Summary: Redwood can implement a 2-hour TTL for session-level KV and derived logs for a trial. Implementation notes: 
- Enforcement: TTL is applied at the storage layer; we can configure per-customer default TTLs and enforce at write path. For active KV caches needed for inference warm starts, we can keep ephemeral in-memory shards and persist nothing beyond the configured TTL.
- Residency: we can pin data storage to a US region (us-west) for the customer’s account and block cross-region replication for logs.
- Audit evidence: we can provide (1) a redacted sample log showing TTL truncation metadata, (2) SOC2 section PDF that references log retention controls (see attached excerpt), and (3) a scripted sample access-log export (CSV) for a 24h window — note that sample will be scrubbed/redacted.

Caveats: 
- Warm start behavior: very short TTLs (<=1h) will reduce cache hit rates and increase median latency for cold workloads. We recommend 2h for the trial to balance latency vs. retention.
- Operational runbook: we should include an automatic fallback policy to a non-PII-prefetching model variant if cache is cold.

I’ll prepare the redacted log sample and SOC2 excerpt as artifacts for Friday. Ben — can you draft the one-paragraph contract addendum that captures the carveout and acceptance criteria?

Karthik
